search_strategy: Very thorough but with one systemic gap. Chat: ran a broad Mattermost full-text search first (python3 /tmp/mm.py <term>, hitting the real search API across ALL channels) for 'planner', then dumped only 8 of the 12 channels whole (pipeline, engineering, code-review, cookbooks, random, viewer, incidents, help — via /tmp/mmdump.py) and ran ~15 rounds of targeted grep -n over those 8 dumps for phrase clusters (plan.json/sidecar/batch_plan, sha256/fingerprint digests, BatchPayloadTooLarge/subclass, auto sizing/max_batches, plan_id/plan_document, total_requests/total_bytes/limits). #general and #releases were never dumped and never independently searched, so any remark seated only there was invisible unless it happened to contain a word the initial broad search used (it never did for the 8 remarks living there). Wiki: fetched all 114 pages individually and walked every comment tree into one greppable file (a thorough, comments-aware sweep — the task's stated trap about BookStack search not indexing comments was correctly worked around). Mail: ran IMAP TEXT searches for planner/batch_size/plan/payload/sizing/fragment/oversize/batch_plan and read every matching thread in full. Within the 8 dumped chat channels, several remarks were still missed because the grep keyword lists, while broad, did not include the specific literal identifiers (e.g. 'num_requests', 'seeded the dir') that those particular remarks used — this cost no facts except in combination with the #general gap. No truncation or crashed helper scripts caused meaningful loss; a few early script bugs (comment-parsing, heredoc/pager issues) were self-corrected within 1-2 steps.
end_reason: Completed normally: work was merged to main (commit 7e63ef7), Gitea Actions CI run #4 for that SHA reports success, and the deployed curator service answered healthy (all three provenance facts = 1, transcript lines 6360-6373). The 0.7 reward reflects 7 of 10 hidden-requirement facts passing; the 3 losses are not from the run dying or CI failing but from one wrong implementation choice (invented top-level JSON key names/order for batch_plan.json) traceable to a genuine corpus-search gap.
notable: Systemic gap: mmdump only fetched 8 of the company's 12 Mattermost channels (missing #general, #releases, #off-topic, #town-square) — line 1254-1266. Every remark seated in #general (3: l11, l15/say22, say22) or #releases (5: l7, say24, say25, rev1, h1) was invisible except by accident of the initial broad search matching unrelated terms.

The exact top-level envelope order/names for batch_plan.json had exactly one direct carrier (g1.r1.say22, #general) plus one redundant carrier of the field NAMES alone (g1.r1.say30, #incidents — dumped, but never grepped for). Missing both caused the agent to invent 'total_requests'/'total_bytes' and the wrong key order at transcript line 4746-4770, which alone accounts for all 3 lost facts (g1.r1.rule, scope, observability) despite everything else about r1 (fingerprint algorithm, per-batch shape, max_batches_per_plan=512, error hierarchy, metadata exclusion) being correctly found and implemented.

A non-plant scaffolding remark (#code-review, 2025-01-23 14:18, dario: 'the fragmentation error... wants to be a BatchPayloadTooLargeError subclass') directly contradicts the real, later-settled decision. The agent read it (line 1689-1691) but was not misled by it — it found and correctly deferred to the later #code-review Apr-8 thread that settles the question the other way, so g1.r1.failure_behavior still passed. This is the kind of task-defect risk described as 'overridden_by_other_corpus_text' that did NOT materialize here.

The agent explicitly noticed the gap it had (line 3644: 'Need exact top-level key names of the plan document... Need more on plan_document shape') and made several further grep attempts to close it (line 3651, 3663) before giving up and shipping a guess — this was a genuine, acknowledged blind spot, not an oversight the agent was unaware of.

All four herrings (2 for r1, 2 for r2) were correctly resisted: the final shipped code uses a standalone batch_plan.json sidecar (not the widened-metadata herring) and sweeps requests_*/metadata_* only after planning succeeds (not the sweep-first herring), matching every reversal the agent did manage to find.
